name: Hue food guide
summary: Start with bún bò Huế at Dong Ba, then cơm hến on Hen Island, then bánh khoái along Kim Long toward Thien Mu. The small cakes and nem lụi follow.
body: Hue eats a beef-and-pork noodle bowl, a clam rice on the river island, and a turmeric crepe on the north bank. It is not mì Quảng and not cao lầu. Those belong down the coast.

Give the first bowl to Dong Ba. Cross Ưng Bình bridge for Hen Island when you want cơm hến or bún hến, and skip the island in a flood week. Kim Long, on the way to Thien Mu, is the road for bánh khoái and bún thịt nướng. Nem lụi is grilled pork on a skewer, wrapped in rice paper with herbs and a creamy sauce.
specialtiesLead: The first bowls and cakes are bún bò Huế, cơm hến, bánh bèo, bánh khoái, bánh nậm, and nem lụi.

sections.heading: Also ordered in Hue
paragraphs: Bún thịt nướng is the Kim Long lunch. Bún hến is the other bowl on Hen Island, beside cơm hến. After the meal, the sweet soups are corn, lotus seed, and taro, with grilled-pork dumplings.

spots.name: Bun thit nuong
spots.note: Cold rice noodles with hot grilled pork, herbs, green papaya, carrot, cucumber, and lettuce. Hue’s peanut sauce and a sweet-sour fish sauce go on the noodles, then you toss.

spots.name: Bun hen
spots.address: Cồn Hến, across Ưng Bình bridge
spots.note: Bún hến is the other bowl on Hen Island, beside cơm hến. The island walk is under half an hour, and the island disappears when the city floods.

spots.name: Corn chè
spots.note: Corn chè is a glutinous sweet soup taken after the meal.

spots.name: Lotus-seed chè
spots.note: Lotus-seed chè is a glutinous sweet soup taken after the meal.

spots.name: Taro chè
spots.note: Taro chè is a sweet soup taken after the meal.

spots.name: Grilled-pork dumplings
spots.note: Grilled-pork dumplings, taken after the meal.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The doors are markets and roads, not a booked room. Dong Ba is the morning market. Hen Island is the clam rice. Kim Long is the snack road toward Thien Mu. Chi Lăng and Bạch Đằng are the afternoon streets on the far side of the island, and the 3 February 2026 plan still shapes them into a night stop with Hoàng Thành and Bao Vinh.

spots.name: Dong Ba Market
spots.caption: The market front, before bánh khoái and bánh bèo.
spots.note: Start here for produce, then the snacks. A bún bò Huế bowl is inside the market.

spots.name: Hen Island
spots.note: Cross Ưng Bình bridge and eat cơm hến or bún hến from the stalls. The walk is under half an hour, and the island disappears when the city floods.

spots.name: Kim Long
spots.address: Kim Long, north bank toward Thien Mu
spots.note: The north-bank road toward Thien Mu, for bánh khoái and bún thịt nướng. Go in the daytime, on the pagoda ride.

spots.name: Chi Lang and Bach Dang
spots.note: The afternoon streets after Hen Island. The 3 February 2026 plan also names them as a night stop still being shaped, with Hoàng Thành and Bao Vinh.
